sampling_model.design: Row-wise i.i.d. sampling from a conditional-IV triangular array with fixed finite \(J\) and \(K\).
sampling_model.units: Observed units are \(O_{ni}=(X_{ni},Z_{ni},D_{ni},S_{ni},S_{ni}Y_{ni})\); potential variables obey the stated IV and principal-stratum restrictions.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary instrument \(Z_{ni}\), binary received treatment \(D_{ni}\), no defiers, and exclusion.
sampling_model.overlap: Covariate-cell and instrument propensities are uniformly bounded away from zero, and only aggregate survivor-complier mass is bounded away from zero.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Every empirical conditional proportion uses the explicit count-denominator fallback in \(\texttt{def:finite-sample-totalization}\). Raw capacities are unscreened, projected onto the nonnegative orthant, and coupled to one Gaussian multiplier draw through the totalized finite-dimensional influence vector; the plug-in quotient uses \(\widehat M_n^{\dagger}=1\) only when its empirical denominator is zero.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Sharp symbolic probability-of-benefit bounds are paired with a study of \(n\)-out-of-\(n\) bootstrap undercoverage at boundary laws and a conservative \(m\)-out-of-\(n\) bootstrap remedy.
Sharp lower and upper bounds on the probability that treatment is beneficial for an ordinal outcome are determined by the two treatment-arm marginal distributions.
Ordinary bootstrap consistency under a Gaussian first-stage limit requires full differentiability, and estimated directional derivatives provide an alternative.
Selected-complier mean-bound estimators are jointly root-\(n\) normal and semiparametrically efficient under trimming regularity, margin, and overlap conditions.
Adaptive inequality selection and Gaussian critical values yield inference for intersection bounds.
Estimated directional derivatives and localized optimizer sets yield uniform inference for optimized value-function statistics.
Randomly perturbed linear programs yield uniform coverage of an outer set and exact coverage on a further outer target.

body.tldr: The completed \(\texttt{pid_slate_benefit_partialtransport}\) theorem supplies the exact selected-complier capacities and closed sharp benefit endpoints as an established input. Every empirical conditional proportion, projected capacity, influence component, multiplier quantile, and confidence interval is totalized on all finite samples by an explicit count-denominator convention, whose activation probability vanishes uniformly. Because the projected piecewise linear-fractional map can change active cuts and survivor support at the \(n^{-1/2}\) scale, the procedure uses an explicit studentized rule with fixed \(\beta_n=1/\log(n+\mathrm e^2)\) to retain every empirically plausible projection, gap, survivor-minimum, cut, and mass-cap face, then calibrates the largest of the two signed endpoint errors with one conditional multiplier process. The main theorem gives uniform root-\(n\) coverage of the entire sharp interval without deterministic padding or an analyst-chosen rate sequence, oracle equivalence recovers ordinary precision on separated faces, the formulas reduce to ordinary ordinal-benefit bounds under perfect compliance and universal selection, and a complete finite atom table supplies a legal changing-support stress test.

project_justification.gap: Existing ordinal-benefit work supplies sharp symbolic bounds and studies ordinary-bootstrap boundary undercoverage with a conservative subsampling remedy, but does not prove uniform no-padding coverage of the entire projected survivor-complier quotient interval. Generic nonsmooth and intersection-bound methods do not directly handle the interacting orthant projection, changing cell support, nested min-cut branches, two signed endpoints, and common denominator.
project_justification.niche: Fixed finite covariate and ordered-outcome supports make every relevant face and gradient explicit, while still permitting the economically important configurations that defeat smooth delta-method inference.
project_justification.fill: Taking the completed exact-capacity and closed-endpoint mapping as fixed, a finite pathwise secant envelope reduces its sampling problem to a common finite Gaussian maximum. Explicit count-based totalization makes the procedure a well-defined map on every sample, while the uniform empty-cell bound shows that this convention is asymptotically invisible. Near-face retention then delivers honest whole-set coverage and adapts to the oracle on separated configurations.

body.related_work: The completed \(\texttt{pid_slate_benefit_partialtransport}\) theorem establishes the exact capacities and closed sharp endpoints used here; those identification results are imported rather than claimed as a contribution. Chen and Flores (2015) motivate the always-employed Job Corps complier stratum and bound its mean wage effect, but their inferential discussion excludes bounding functions with nested minimum and maximum operators. Lu, Ding, and Dasgupta (2018) give ordinary sharp ordinal-benefit bounds, recovered here under perfect compliance and universal selection. Gabriel, Sachs, and Jensen (2024) give sharp symbolic ordinal-benefit bounds, document \(n\)-out-of-\(n\) bootstrap undercoverage at boundary laws, and use a conservative \(m\)-out-of-\(n\) remedy; the narrower missing result is uniform no-padding coverage of the whole projected survivor-complier quotient interval. Dong and Heiler (2026) derive efficient orthogonal inference for selected-complier mean bounds, but their smooth trimming and relevant-support conditions do not cover discrete ordered atoms or disappearing cell survivor masses. Fang and Santos (2019) explain why ordinary resampling fails for nonlinear directional derivatives and motivate resampling an estimated local derivative. Chernozhukov, Lee, and Rosen (2013), Andrews and Soares (2010), and Andrews and Barwick (2012) motivate retaining near-binding faces. Firpo, Galvao, and Parker (2023) show how localized optimizer sets enter value-function inference. Hsieh, Shi, and Shum (2022) and Cho and Russell (2024) provide optimization-based alternatives, but their procedures do not yield the explicit no-latent-program critical value for this exact whole identified set. Standard multinomial asymptotics are usually written on the event of nonempty conditioning cells; the finite-cell and instrument-overlap conditions here additionally yield an explicit uniform exponential bound for the complement, making all reported empirical and multiplier objects total on finite samples.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The complete law \(P_n^{\mathrm{wit}}\) is a boundary stress test, not a theorem that any named published implementation undercovers. Numerical experiments with empirical optimizer-only and survivor-positive screening indicate sensitivity to discarded projection, cut, survivor-minimum, mass-cap, and denominator directions, but no published procedure has been verified to use exactly that composite shortcut. Accordingly no strict single-face undercoverage probability is claimed. Finite multiplier simulation error is also outside the exact-conditional-quantile theorem.
body.honest_scope: The proposal fixes \(J\) and \(K\), assumes aggregate survivor-complier mass and the nonredundant raw-capacity covariance remain bounded away from zero, and uses the nonnegative-orthant projection. It imposes no lower bound on an individual cell survivor mass, no survivor-gap sign margin, and no cut separation in the main theorem. The exact capacity and closed sharp-endpoint theorem \(\texttt{pid_slate_benefit_partialtransport}\) is an established input and is not in the to-prove contribution graph. Every empirical object is defined on all finite samples by the stated denominator fallbacks, and the probability that any such fallback is activated vanishes uniformly. The contribution is uniform no-padding whole-set inference for the imported mapping together with a fully specified studentized face-retention rule requiring no analyst-chosen rate sequence; the smooth unique-face and perfect-compliance reductions are corollaries, and the finite atom array is a methodological stress test rather than an undercoverage claim. Continuous covariates, weak aggregate denominators, and simulated-quantile error are outside scope.
